newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Rains pick up in Ivorian cocoa areas, favour crop.
newsitem.headline: Rains pick up in Ivorian cocoa areas, favour crop.

text.p: Rains strengthened in Ivorian cocoa areas in late July after a drier than normal start to the July-August dry season, favouring crop prospects for 1997/98 (Oct-Sept), weather and crop analysts saId on Tuesday.
"There has been a rain deficit for this month," said a national weather centre spokesman.
But crop analysts said pod development was unaffected by low rainfall earlier in July as soil moisture had been kept up by cool temperatures, blanket cloud and torrential June rains.
A dry July in 1994 had not had an adverse impact on developing main crops (April-Sept) that year, one said.
Official national weather data for the last 10 days of July show rains averaged 20.8 mm at 10 monitored stations, against 14.8 mm in the previous 10 days and 16.7 mm in the 10 day period before that.
Main crop estimates for 1997/98 (Oct-April) are expected to reach traders over the next couple of weeks as pod-counters return from scrutinising trees for a clue to harvest size.
French-Swiss chocolate-maker Barry Callebaut, which has two factories in Ivory Coast, has predicted a 1997/98 crop of 1.1 million tonnes.
London broker GNI said in a recent report the crop could top 1.2 million tonnes -- the size of the 1995/96 record harvest -- if weather remained favourable.
An El Nino weather pattern could bring dry weather to West Africa in late 1997 and have an effect on the generally smaller 1997/98 mid crop (May-Sept).
Main crops need light regular showers and patchy sunlight in July and August.

The latest weather data, from Ivory Coast's national weather station, showed the following rainfall (mm) for the last 10 days of July in key growing areas plus the commercial capital Abidjan (previous 10 days bracketed).
Daloa 8.9 (86.5), Gagnoa 6.3 (4.4), San Pedro 12.6 (0), Tabou 11.3 (33.0), Man 56.2 (14.4), Dimbokro 35.5 (6.6), Yamoussoukro 23.8 (0.6), Abidjan 8.4 (0), Sassandra 25.4 (0), Adiake 19.3 (2.9).
